News Around

1

Solomon F. Sopher, a prominent and enthusiastic racehorse owner for over five decades, passed away today, Tuesday, 3 November 2026, in Mumbai.

Solomon F. Sopher was the President of the Baghdadi Jewish community in Mumbai, India. He also served as a Trustee of the David Sassoon Fund and as Chairman and Managing Director of the Sir Jacob Sassoon Trust, which manages the Knesset Eliyahoo Synagogue in Mumbai, as well as the Magen David and Ohel David Synagogues in Pune.

He was also associated with several other Jewish institutions, serving as a Trustee and Chairman of organisations such as E.E.E. Sassoon High School, Sassoon Guest House, David Sassoon Library, Lady Rachel Sassoon Dispensary, Sassoon Dock and the Indian Jewish Federation, among others.

May his soul rest in peace. Indiarace extends its heartfelt condolences to the bereaved family.

2

At the Meeting of the Members of the Managing Committee of the Bangalore Turf Club Ltd, held on Monday 2nd November 2026 at 6.30 PM, Mr Arvind S Katarki was unanimously elected as the chairman & senior Steward of the Bangalore Turf Club Ltd for the year 2026-27.

3

A group 3 winner Royal Rhyme (IRE) by Lope De Vega (IRE) ex Dubai Queen (USA) will stand at Hazara Stud Farm in Haryana. The deal brokered by Ajay Anne.

4

Nations Pride(IRE) by Teofilo(IRE) out of Important Time(IRE), a four time Gr.1 winner will retire to the Sohna Stud Farm in a deal brokered by Ajay Anne. Nations Pride will join the Stallion Planetaire(GB) & Portamento(IRE) for the 2027 breeding season.

5

Four time Group 1 winner Sosie (IRE) by Sea The Stars ex Sosia will retire to the Poonawalla Stud Farms. Sosie will join the stallions Territories (IRE), Satono Impresa (JPN) and Leitir Mor (IRE) for the 2027 breeding season.

6

Nelson Reuben sadly passed away earlier today in Calcutta. He was undoubtedly one of the greatest jockeys to have graced the Calcutta turf in the seventies and eighties. His unique style of horsemanship fetched him classics galore. Perhaps the one most recalled by oldtimers was his victory atop Topmost in the Indian Derby of 1974. Nelson lived up to his name and enjoyed a huge fan following all over the country during an era  when  Calcutta jockeys ruled the roost- his contemporaries Robin Corner and Richard Alford to name a couple of others. Nelson will always be remembered fondly by local railbirds.

7

Finally Btc has got the license to conduct offcourse betting. It's a part time license, only from Sept 1 to 16. It will be renewed once the club agrees to the conditions of the government regarding the shifting and the compromise petition before the supreme court in its egm on Sept 16. It's a big relief from btc's point of view and hopefully all goes well and racing continues after Sept 16 too.
